newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to let private firms run T$350b state funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to let private firms run T$350b state funds.

text.p: Taiwan's top economic policymaking agency said on Wednesday it has decided to commission private fund management firms to manage some T$350 billion worth of state funds.

"This will help promote Taiwan to become a regional asset-management centre and help upgrade institutional investors' investment ratio in the stock and bond markets," an official at the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said by telephone.
Relevant government agencies reached an agreement at a meeting on Tuesday to revise rules by the end of December to allow private management of state funds, he said.
The decision is expected to allow more flexible and efficient operations of state funds and expand their investments in stock and bond markets, the official said.

Currently, the state funds total some T$350 billion, including T$200 billion worth of labour insurance funds, T$110 billion worth of labour pension funds, and T$40 billion of state employee pension funds, he said.
At present, these state funds are allowed to invest up to 30 percent of their holdings in stocks.
